paragraphs.text: A DeepSeek Harness plugin: global search across session content, ordered by content time.
# dsh-session-search
**English** | 中文

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that searches the
**content** of every session — not just session titles —

and orders hits by the **time of the
matched record**, newest first.

It adds a first-class search destination to the sidebar (a panel icon beside *Plugins* and
*Schedule

s*, plus a full-width results page) and a `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F` shortcut. Clicking a hit
opens its sess

plus a full-width results page) and a `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F` shortcut. Clicking a hit
opens its session.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why this plugin exists

Stock DSH can already *search* sessions — the sidebar search box is wired to a real
content-search p

H can already *search* sessions — the sidebar search box is wired to a real
content-search pipeline:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It only ever finds titles because **three independent things** are true at once:
| # | Fact | Where |
| 1 | The content backend is **switched off** in the stock profile — `openAt: never`. The shipped co
mment says it plainly: *"the Web sidebar search matches titles and workspace names only."* | the `se

ssion-query-sqlite` row in `dsh-base/cordis.patch.yml` |
| 2 | That backend tokenizes with FTS5 `uni
code61`, which treats **an entire CJK run as a single token**. Measured on a real machine: `光速太慢，星际文
明无法成为整体` yields exactly two tokens, `光速太慢` and `星际文明无法成为整体` — so `MATCH '光速'` and `MATCH '星际'` both
**return nothing**. The `trigram` tokenizer is no help either: it rejects 2-character queries. | ver

ified locally against SQLite 3.53.4 |
| 3 | Even with the backend enabled, the wire shape is `{ item
s: [{ sessionId, snippet }] }` — **each hit's `time` is dropped at that layer**, and ranking is rele
vance-first (`time` is only a tie-breaker). | `dsh-api-session-controller/lib/index.js` |

So "order results by content time" is **not achievable through any shipped public remote**, and
for

CJK content the shipped engine is the wrong tool regardless. This plugin therefore builds its
own in

dex on the host: it incrementally parses every session transcript, keeps each record's text
together

with **that record's own `time`**, matches by substring (correct for both CJK and Latin
text), and
sorts by time. It needs **no profile configuration changes**.
## Where the search entry lives — and why

DSH's Web/desktop UI has **no global top bar** and **no global command palette** (`/` commands are
t

he composer's slash menu and are bound to the current session). Only three global seats are
availabl

composer's slash menu and are bound to the current session). Only three global seats are
available:
| Seat | Verdict |
| **`sidebar.panellist` icon + its matching `main` panel** | ✅ **Used here.** This is DSH's first-cl
ass "global panel" mechanism: the sidebar owns the button, the label and the selected state, and the
list `id` maps directly to the `main` panel `key`. The shipped **Plugins** (order 0) and **Schedule
s** (order 10) panels work exactly this way; this plugin slots in between at order 5. `replaceRisk:

none` — it cannot be clobbered by an upgrade. |
| `sidebar.footer.action` (next to Settings) + a `sh
ell.overlay` dialog | ⭕ Viable alternative, better suited to a "spotlight" quick-search. Costs you h

and-built overlay, focus and Escape handling, and leaves little room for snippets. |
| `sidebar.work
spaces` (where the existing search box lives) | ❌ **Not used.** It is a `single` seat occupied whole
sale by `ui-workspace`, with `replaceRisk: shadows-shipped-ui` — taking it means replacing the entir
e shipped session browser and breaking on the next DSH release. |
A **`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F`** shortcut (registered through `dsh-client-shortcuts`) selects the panel from
anywhere. It is bound on the **desktop profiles only** on purpose: on the Web profiles the shipped

`session.fork` (`dsh-client-ui-workspace`) already owns `KeyF + primary+shift`, and the shortcut
reg

istry validates a definition's defaults across every *declared* profile, throwing
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility

Built and verified against **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2** (Electron 44.7.0, `@deepseek-ai/cordis`
4
.0.5). It has no runtime dependency on any Harness package, so only the documented service and slot

runtime dependency on any Harness package, so only the documented service and slot
contracts matter.

**0.2.1-rc.2 incident — fixed in 0.1.1.** Version 0.1.0 also registered `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F` on the
We

b profiles. 0.2.1-rc.2 ships `session.fork` in `dsh-client-ui-workspace` bound to
`KeyF + primary+sh

ift` on Web, and `dsh-client-shortcuts` validates a definition's defaults across
every declared prof

ile, throwing `Conflicting shortcut defaults` from whichever plugin registers
second. That was `ui-w

orkspace`: its failure left 16 client entries waiting for the `uiWorkspace`
service and turned the r

enderer boot into a fatal `web boot: 17 entries did not activate`. DSH's
crash recovery then sanitiz
ed the profile back to its default bundle list.
0.1.1 binds **desktop profiles only** and guards the registration, so a future release re-binding th

e
combination costs this panel its shortcut — never the application's boot. If you installed 0.1.0,
update and re-install the bundle.
## Known limitations

- **The find bar only reaches rendered content.** The chat virtualizer keeps a window of turns in
th

e DOM, so `Ctrl/Cmd+F` (like a browser's find-in-page) sees only what is rendered; *Search all
histo

ry* in the bar, or the indexed dialog, covers the rest. Deep links to an event sequence are
still im

possible: `ChatNavigation.navigateToTurn` / `input.loadThrough(seq)` are private to the
chat panel.
- The keyboard shortcut is **desktop-only**; Web profiles stay unbound so the plugin cannot collide

with a shipped Web binding (see Compatibility). The sidebar icon always works.
- The index lives in

memory for the lifetime of the Host process; it is not persisted to disk (a
cold build is ~1.2 s, no

rmally invisible).
- Matching is **substring**, not tokenized and not semantic. Multiple whitespace-

separated terms are
ANDed.
- Text beyond `maxCharsPerRecord` (default 64 KiB) in a single record is

truncated.
- The official SQLite FTS backend stays disabled. This plugin deliberately does **not** e

nable it:
even enabled, it cannot match CJK substrings (see fact #2 above). If you would rather have

the
official backend with relevance ranking, that is a separate configuration change and not someth

ing
a plugin can do.
